Theme

Construction, trades & building materials

tie verb

also lash, bind, tie up, tie back, tie in a knot, knot

classical

Digest 13.6.5.7: māchinae … nōn ab ipsō ligātae
Traupman 394

ligō, ligāre, ligāvī, ligātum

verb, first conjugation

tie, lash

The Digest’s verb for a Roman scaffold.

Other words

  • nōdō, nōdāre, nōdāvī, nōdātum — tie in a knot, knot

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 4.138: crīnēs nōdantur in aurum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 394

  • alligō, alligāre, alligāvī, alligātum — tie (to something), bind fast

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.71: ad pālum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 394

  • revinciō, revincīre, revīnxī, revīnctum — tie back, bind behind; bind fast

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.13: ancorae prō fūnibus ferreīs catēnīs revīnctae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 394

    Lewis & Short: classical, but not in Cicero.

  • vinciō, vincīre, vīnxī, vīnctum — bind, tie up; put in bonds

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.170: facinus est vincīre cīvem Rōmānum (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.53: trīnīs catēnīs vīnctus (Lewis & Short)

  • nectō, nectere, nexuī (nexī), nexum — bind, tie, fasten together; weave together

    conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. E. 8.77: necte tribus nōdīs ternōs, Amarylli, colōrēs (Lewis & Short); Liv. 8.28 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Vincula calceōrum ligēmus.

    Let’s tie the shoelaces.composed

  • facinus est vincīre cīvem Rōmānum

    it is a crime to put a Roman citizen in bondsCic. Verr. 2.5.170 (Lewis & Short)

  • necte tribus nōdīs ternōs, Amarylli, colōrēs

    tie the three colours, Amaryllis, in three knotsVerg. E. 8.77 (Lewis & Short)

See also scaffold tie, secure, scaffold, knot, undo, shoelace.
